title: Machine-Readable Dutch Law Schema v0.6.0
description: Article-based schema for machine-readable representation of Dutch laws and regulations.

name.description: Name of the law/regulation (can be plain text or internal reference like '#wet_naam').

publication_date.description: Date when the law/regulation was officially published (publicatiedatum).

valid_from.description: Date when the law/regulation becomes effective (inwerkingtredingsdatum), or an internal reference starting with #.

valid_to.description: Last calendar day on which the law/regulation is in force, inclusive (einddatum). Set ONLY when the law is terminated - it vervalt or wordt ingetrokken (a horizonbepaling/vervalbepaling, or repeal by another instrument); omit when a newer version of the same law simply takes over. A statutory 'vervalt met ingang van D' maps to valid_to = D minus one day. Must be a literal date (no internal references): the engine reads it as static version-selection metadata; end dates derived from another instrument or an executed article output are future work. See RFC-019.

regulatory_layer.description: Type of legal instrument (regelgevingslaag). It fixes which identifier the file must carry, and it ranks candidates when several regulations implement the same open term. Which layer may implement a term is set by that term's `delegation_type`, not by this field alone.

url.description: Official URL of the law text this file was written from, at the version stated in `valid_from`.

bwb_id.description: BWB identification number (for Dutch national laws).

celex_nummer.description: CELEX number (for EU regulations and directives).

unts_nummer.description: UN Treaty Series number (for international treaties).

waterschap_code.description: CBS water board code (for water board regulations).

organisation.description: Organization responsible (for implementation policies without official IDs).

legal_basis.description: Articles of higher law that authorize this regulation: the grondslag. Not the same shape as the `legal_basis` a field or action carries, which cites a provision far more precisely.

law_id.description: Identifier of the law that provides authority.

article.description: Article number that authorizes this regulation.

description.description: Optional explanation of the legal relationship.

preamble.description: The aanhef, the passage before Article 1 that names the authority the regulation is made under. It carries no operative norm of its own, so it rarely computes anything.

text.description: Preamble text in markdown format, preserving original formatting from official publication.

url.description: URL to the preamble in the official publication (if available).

machine_readable.description: Machine-readable interpretation of the preamble, in the same shape as an article's. A preamble rarely computes anything; it most often carries `legal_basis` and the `competent_authority` for the whole regulation.

articles.description: The articles of this regulation, in the order they appear in the law. An article is carried as text whether or not it has been translated; `machine_readable` is what makes one executable.

number.description: Article number as it appears in the law.

text.description: Article text in markdown format, preserving original formatting from official publication (numbered lists, links, paragraph structure).

machine_readable.description: Machine-readable interpretation of this article. Absent when the article has not been translated, which is the normal state for most of the corpus: an article without this key is carried as text only.

references.description: Structured references to other laws/articles for runtime resolution.

id.description: Reference ID used in markdown links (e.g., 'ref1').

procedure.description: AWB-defined procedure lifecycles for administrative decisions (RFC-008).

default.description: Whether this is the default procedure for its legal_character.

applies_to.description: The output this procedure governs, naming the article and the output within it whose besluit runs through these stages.

requires.description: External inputs required to enter this stage.

name.description: Name of the value this stage needs before it can complete.

type.description: Value type of the required input.

stages.description: The lifecycle stages in order, from the application to the final decision. Each stage names the Awb article that sets its term.

name.description: Field name, referenced elsewhere as `$name`. This is the name another law asks for when it reads this value through `source`, so renaming an output is a change other laws can see.

type.description: Value type. What an `amount` is counted in is declared separately, in `type_spec.unit`; units are opt-in per law, and an un-annotated value has unit `unknown` and is never checked (RFC-023).

nullable.description: Whether `null` (absence: the register or the law says there is none) is a legitimate value of this field. Defaults to false: a non-nullable input may never receive null from a data source, another law or a caller, a non-nullable output may never evaluate to null, and a non-nullable parameter may never be passed null. On a required parameter the flag means the same at the top level and across laws: a nullable one is run with the null and decides on it, a non-nullable one is a caller error at the top level and skips the call across laws. Unknown (a value nobody has) is not governed by this flag. RFC-036.

type_spec.description: Additional type specifications for numeric and temporal values.

unit.description: Unit of measurement for the value (RFC-023). A label, never a computational constraint: tagging a value never changes it. `ratio` (0-1) and `percentage` (0-100) are distinct labels; any division by 100 is an explicit value operation, never implied by the label.

precision.description: Number of decimal places for numeric values.

temporal.description: How the value relates to time: whether it is measured at a moment or over a period, and which date it is anchored to (RFC-001). Declared in the schema but not yet read by the engine, and unused in the corpus.

type.description: Whether the value represents a period or point in time.

period_type.description: Granularity of the period (for period type).

legal_basis.description: The provision this field rests on. On an output it is the article granting the entitlement; on an input, the provision that makes the value relevant.

variableReference.description: Variable reference starting with $ (e.g., $standaardpremie, $referencedate.year). Supports dot notation for property access.

required.description: Whether the caller must pass this parameter. Defaults to true: an omitted required parameter is an error. A parameter declared `required: false` that the caller omits resolves to an unknown value that names the parameter (RFC-036), so a law can declare application-form fields another law never passes.

source.description: Reference to where this input comes from.

regulation.description: Name of external law/regulation. Omit for external data sources that must be resolved outside the YAML.

output.description: Output name to retrieve from the source.

parameters.description: Parameters passed when calling the source regulation. A map from the parameter name the source expects to the value passed for it, usually a `$`-reference to a value in scope, as in `bsn: $bsn`.

description.description: Human-readable description or legal reference for this data source.

endpoint.description: Endpoint to call on the delegated regulation.

arithmeticOperation.description: Arithmetic operations that compute numeric values.

operation.description: Operation discriminator. Pins this object to the ADD / SUBTRACT / MULTIPLY / DIVIDE / MIN / MAX form; the engine dispatches on it and the schema rejects any other key combination.

legal_basis.description: The article this particular step rests on. Set it where one action combines rules from several provisions and the operands come from different articles, so a trace can name the provision behind each step.

logicalOperation.description: Logical operations that combine boolean conditions.

operation.description: Operation discriminator. Pins this object to the AND / OR form; the engine dispatches on it and the schema rejects any other key combination.

conditions.description: Conditions to combine - each item can be an operation, variable reference, or boolean literal.

legal_basis.description: The article this particular step rests on. Set it where one action combines rules from several provisions and the operands come from different articles, so a trace can name the provision behind each step.

comparisonOperation.description: Comparison operations that compare values. Operands may be numbers or ISO 8601 dates (YYYY-MM-DD); when both operands are dates they are compared chronologically (RFC-021).

operation.description: Operation discriminator. Pins this object to the EQUALS / GREATER_THAN / LESS_THAN / GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL / LESS_THAN_OR_EQUAL form; the engine dispatches on it and the schema rejects any other key combination.

subject.description: The value being compared, on the left of the comparison.

value.description: The value compared against, on the right of the comparison.

legal_basis.description: The article this particular step rests on. Set it where one action combines rules from several provisions and the operands come from different articles, so a trace can name the provision behind each step.

notOperation.description: Logical NOT - negates a boolean value.

operation.description: Operation discriminator. Pins this object to the NOT form; the engine dispatches on it and the schema rejects any other key combination.

legal_basis.description: The article this particular step rests on. Set it where one action combines rules from several provisions and the operands come from different articles, so a trace can name the provision behind each step.

roundingOperation.description: Rounding operations (RFC-024). Round the single operand to `precision` decimal places, in the value's own unit (RFC-023). Rounding is never implicit - a law that rounds must say so here. ROUND is half-up (rekenkundig, the Hoge Raad default); CEIL rounds up (naar boven); FLOOR rounds down (naar beneden / afkapping).

operation.description: Operation discriminator. Pins this object to the ROUND / CEIL / FLOOR form; the engine dispatches on it and the schema rejects any other key combination.

precision.description: Number of decimal places to round to, in the value's own unit. 0 = whole units; 2 = two decimals; a negative value rounds to tens/hundreds (e.g. -2 rounds a eurocent value to whole euros).

legal_basis.description: The article this particular step rests on. Set it where one action combines rules from several provisions and the operands come from different articles, so a trace can name the provision behind each step.

ifOperation.description: Conditional operation with multiple cases evaluated in order.

operation.description: Operation discriminator. Pins this object to the IF form; the engine dispatches on it and the schema rejects any other key combination.

cases.description: Cases evaluated in order; the first whose `when` holds decides the value. Order is significant, so a narrower case belongs before a broader one.

default.description: Value when no case matches. Without it, an IF whose cases all fail evaluates to null (absence, RFC-036), so the validator refuses a defaultless IF on an output that is not `nullable`. A case whose condition is unknown takes neither its branch nor the default.

legal_basis.description: The article this particular step rests on. Set it where one action combines rules from several provisions and the operands come from different articles, so a trace can name the provision behind each step.

inOperation.description: Membership test - checks if subject is in a list.

operation.description: Operation discriminator. Pins this object to the IN form; the engine dispatches on it and the schema rejects any other key combination.

value.description: A single value or a reference to a list to test against. Use `values` instead to write the list inline.

legal_basis.description: The article this particular step rests on. Set it where one action combines rules from several provisions and the operands come from different articles, so a trace can name the provision behind each step.

operation.description: Operation discriminator. Pins this object to the LIST form; the engine dispatches on it and the schema rejects any other key combination.

legal_basis.description: The article this particular step rests on. Set it where one action combines rules from several provisions and the operands come from different articles, so a trace can name the provision behind each step.

foreachOperation.description: Iterate over a collection, evaluating an expression per element (RFC-016).

operation.description: Operation discriminator. Pins this object to the FOREACH form; the engine dispatches on it and the schema rejects any other key combination.

collection.description: Expression evaluating to the array to iterate over. A non-array iterates as a single element; null is an empty collection.

as.description: Name of the local variable bound to the current element. Defaults to 'item'.

filter.description: Evaluated per element in the child scope; elements for which it is false are skipped.

body.description: Evaluated once per surviving element, in the child scope where 'as' is bound.

combine.description: Aggregation over the collected results. Omitted, the results are returned as an array.

legal_basis.description: The article this particular step rests on. Set it where one action combines rules from several provisions and the operands come from different articles, so a trace can name the provision behind each step.

ageOperation.description: Calculate age in complete years between two dates.

operation.description: Operation discriminator. Pins this object to the AGE form; the engine dispatches on it and the schema rejects any other key combination.

reference_date.description: Reference date to calculate age at.

legal_basis.description: The article this particular step rests on. Set it where one action combines rules from several provisions and the operands come from different articles, so a trace can name the provision behind each step.

dateAddOperation.description: Add years, months, weeks, and/or days to a date. Applied coarsest-to-finest: years → months → weeks → days. Month/year additions use the Dutch legal 'corresponding numbered day' rule: the day is clamped to the last day of the target month (e.g., Jan 31 + 1 month = Feb 28).

operation.description: Operation discriminator. Pins this object to the DATE_ADD form; the engine dispatches on it and the schema rejects any other key combination.

years.description: Number of years to add (clamped to last day of target month).

months.description: Number of months to add (clamped to last day of target month).

legal_basis.description: The article this particular step rests on. Set it where one action combines rules from several provisions and the operands come from different articles, so a trace can name the provision behind each step.

dateConstructOperation.description: Construct a date from year, month, day components.

operation.description: Operation discriminator. Pins this object to the DATE form; the engine dispatches on it and the schema rejects any other key combination.

legal_basis.description: The article this particular step rests on. Set it where one action combines rules from several provisions and the operands come from different articles, so a trace can name the provision behind each step.

dayOfWeekOperation.description: Get the day of the week (0=Monday, 6=Sunday).

operation.description: Operation discriminator. Pins this object to the DAY_OF_WEEK form; the engine dispatches on it and the schema rejects any other key combination.

legal_basis.description: The article this particular step rests on. Set it where one action combines rules from several provisions and the operands come from different articles, so a trace can name the provision behind each step.

dateDiffOperation.description: Signed difference between two dates, expressed in a chosen unit. Positive when 'to' is on or after 'from'. Months and years count complete calendar units (RFC-021).

operation.description: Operation discriminator. Pins this object to the DATE_DIFF form; the engine dispatches on it and the schema rejects any other key combination.

in.description: Unit the difference is expressed in: 'days', 'months', or 'years' (or a variable resolving to one of these).

legal_basis.description: The article this particular step rests on. Set it where one action combines rules from several provisions and the operands come from different articles, so a trace can name the provision behind each step.

operationType.description: Operation type identifier used in action definitions, naming the same forms the operations below accept.

operation.description: An executable operation that computes a value. Operations nest: any operand may itself be an operation.

output.description: Name of the output field this action computes.

value.description: A literal value for this output, used where the law states an amount or a term outright. When the action also carries an `operation`, that operation wins and this field is read as one of its operands.

operation.description: The operation computing this action's value. Mutually exclusive with `value`: an action either states a literal or computes one.

precision.description: Decimal places for an inline rounding operation (ROUND/CEIL/FLOOR; RFC-024), in the value's own unit. 0 = whole units; negative rounds to tens/hundreds.

resolve.description: Look up the value in whichever regulation implements it. Accepted by the schema, but the Rust law-model has no field for it and drops it on load; no law in the corpus uses it.

type.description: Regulatory layer to search for implementation.

match.description: Matching criteria for selecting the right implementation.

legal_basis.description: The provision this action rests on. Accepted by the schema, but the Rust law-model has no field for it and drops it on load, so it does not reach a trace today.

juriconnect.description: Juriconnect BWB 1.3 reference. Optionally pinned to a date with the `z=`/`g=` parameters; most references in the corpus carry them, and the pattern does not require them.

explanation.description: Dutch explanation of how this element relates to the law text.

examples.explanation: De aanspraak op zorgtoeslag volgt uit artikel 2, eerste lid.

endpoint.description: Named endpoint for this article, making it callable from other regulations.

competent_authority.description: Bevoegd gezag: the authority whose execution of this article produces a binding decision. Another body may run the same calculation and get the same number, but its result carries no legal force (RFC-009). Annotation only: the engine computes the same either way.

type.description: INSTANCE = specific organization (default), CATEGORY = must be resolved per context.

enables.description: What this article enables - e.g., authority to create lower-level regulations.

regulatory_layer.description: Type of regulation this article enables.

subject.description: Subject matter of the enabled regulation (e.g., 'rioolheffing').

for.description: Who is granted the authority (optional - often implied by regulatory_layer).

name.description: Name of the body the enabled regulation is addressed to.

type.description: INSTANCE names one specific body; CATEGORY names a class of bodies that must be resolved per context (every municipality, say).

interface.description: Interface contract that implementing regulations must follow.

name.description: Parameter name the enabled regulation is expected to accept.

required.description: Whether the enabled regulation must be given this parameter.

description.description: What the parameter means, for the author of the enabled regulation.

output.description: Required output fields for the interface.

name.description: Output name the enabled regulation is expected to produce.

description.description: What the output means, for the author of the enabled regulation.

defaults.description: Default execution logic if no implementing regulation is found.

requires.description: Dependencies on other articles, regelingen, or external sources.

values.description: The outputs this article needs from the dependency, named so the dependency is checkable rather than implied.

open_terms.description: Abstract values that must or may be filled by implementing regulations at a lower level. Any regulatory layer can declare open_terms; a law typically has required: true (no default), lower layers often provide defaults that can be refined further down.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this term represents.

type.description: Data type of the expected value.

required.description: Whether an implementation is mandatory (true) or optional with possible default (false).

delegated_to.description: Who is authorized to fill this term (e.g., 'minister', 'gemeenteraad').

delegation_type.description: Expected regulatory layer of the implementation (e.g., 'MINISTERIELE_REGELING').

legal_basis.description: The provision that delegates this term, as it reads in the law (e.g. 'artikel 4 Wet op de zorgtoeslag').

default.description: Default execution logic when no implementing regulation is found. Makes the article executable standalone while still allowing refinement via implements.

implements.description: Declares that this article fills open terms from a higher-level law. Maps to the 'Gelet op' clause in Dutch legislation. One article can implement multiple open terms from different laws.

law.description: The $id of the higher-level law being implemented (e.g., 'wet_op_de_zorgtoeslag').

article.description: Article number in the higher law that declares the open_term (e.g., '4').

gelet_op.description: Legal reference text (e.g., 'Gelet op artikel 4 van de Wet op de zorgtoeslag').

examples.gelet_op: Gelet op artikel 4 van de Wet op de zorgtoeslag

definitions.description: Definitions and constants. Each entry is either a bare value (`naam: 123`) or the optionally-structured form carrying a `type` and `type_spec` so the constant can declare its quantity-kind (RFC-023): `naam: {value: 123, type: amount, type_spec: {unit: eurocent}}`.

execution.description: The executable logic of this article: what it needs, what it computes and what it yields.

legal_character.description: Legal character of the output. BESCHIKKING: a besluit not of general scope (Awb art. 1:3 lid 2). RECHTSPOSITIE: a legal position of a person that arises by operation of law, without a besluit and without an aanvraag (voting rights, majority, nationality).

decision_type.description: The kind of decision this output is, within its legal character. `GEEN_BESLUIT` is the value for an article that establishes a fact rather than deciding anything.

procedure_id.description: Selects a specific AWB procedure variant. When absent, the default procedure for the legal_character is used.

produces.description: What executing this article yields in legal terms: its legal character, the kind of decision it is, and the procedure that governs it. Annotation for the reader and for portals deciding what to offer; it does not change the computed value.

parameters.description: Values the caller passes in, such as a bsn or a peildatum.

input.description: Values this article reads from elsewhere: another law's output, or a fact from a register. Each declares a `source`.

output.description: Values this article yields. Each is callable from another law by name.

actions.description: The steps that compute the outputs, each assigning one output either a literal or the result of an operation.

hooks.description: Hook declarations: this article fires when matching lifecycle events occur (RFC-007).

hook_point.description: Where in the lifecycle of another article's decision this one runs: before its actions or after them.

legal_character.description: Match articles that produce this legal character.

decision_type.description: Optionally narrow to a specific decision type.

stage.description: Lifecycle stage at which this hook fires (e.g., BESLUIT, BEKENDMAKING). Defaults to BESLUIT.

applies_to.description: Which outputs this hook fires for, filtered by legal character and/or decision type. A hook with no filter applies to every output of the article.

overrides.description: Override declarations: this article replaces another article's output (RFC-007, lex specialis).

law.description: The `$id` of the law whose output is being replaced: lex specialis written down. The override fires only when the overriding law is the law being executed, so with no such context it does not apply. The engine does not check that the override is legally valid (RFC-007).

untranslatables.description: Legal constructs in this article that the engine cannot yet express faithfully (RFC-012). Untranslatable means not yet, not never: each entry names a gap in the engine, never a defect in the law, and reads as a concrete feature request recorded at the article that needs it. An article may carry untranslatables and still execute the parts that are expressible. Publishing the gaps is deliberate, so a reader can see where interpretation still happens outside the format rather than having to infer it from an approximation.

construct.description: The legal construct that cannot be translated yet, named in the law's own words (e.g. 'afronden op hele euro's').

reason.description: Which capability the engine is missing, stated as a property of the engine rather than of the law.

suggestion.description: The operation or schema feature that would close the gap. This is what makes the entry actionable: it points at what to build next. Twice now an entry here named an operation the engine went on to gain, rounding (RFC-024) and FOREACH (RFC-016).

legal_text_excerpt.description: The passage from the article that cannot be expressed, quoted verbatim so a reader can judge the gap without opening the law.

accepted.description: Whether a human has reviewed and acknowledged this gap. Accepted untranslatables are allowed in error mode.
